questions.question: What is 'In-Memory OLTP' (Hekaton)?

options.A: A way to run SQL Server entirely on a USB thumb drive.
options.B: A memory-optimized engine integrated into SQL Server for high-concurrency transaction processing.
options.C: A caching tool for SSD drives.
options.D: A feature that stores query results in the user's browser cache.

questions.question: What is 'Log Sequence Number' (LSN)?

options.A: The serial number of the SQL Server software license.
options.B: A unique identifier assigned to every record in the transaction log.
options.C: The number of users currently logged into the server.
options.D: A code used to encrypt database backups.

questions.question: Which DMV is best for seeing the text of a currently executing SQL statement?

options.B: sys.dm_os_schedulers

questions.question: What does 'MAXDOP' stand for?

options.B: Maximum Degree of Parallelism.

questions.question: What is a 'Trivial Plan'?

options.A: A plan generated for a query that is so simple that only one viable execution path exists.
options.B: An incorrect execution plan caused by missing statistics.
options.C: A plan that is only used for temporary tables.
options.D: A security plan used for guest users.

questions.question: How do 'Filtered Indexes' help performance?

options.A: They remove bad data from the database.
options.B: They index only a subset of rows, saving space and improving maintenance and query speed.
options.C: They automatically filter out SQL injection attempts.
options.D: They allow indexes to be used by multiple different databases.

questions.question: What is 'Dirty Page' in buffer management?

options.A: A page that contains illegal characters.
options.B: A data page that has been modified in memory but not yet written to disk.
options.C: A page that has been corrupted by a hardware failure.
options.D: A page that belongs to a deleted table.

questions.question: What is 'Page Split' in an index?

options.A: When an index is divided into two for load balancing.
options.B: When an 8KB page is full and must be split into two pages to accommodate new data.
options.C: When a query result set is too large to fit in one page.
options.D: A method to compress data by 50%.

questions.question: Which DMV identifies missing indexes that could improve performance?

options.B: sys.dm_os_performance_counters

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Indirect Checkpoints'?

options.A: To check user permissions indirectly through roles.
options.B: To provide a target recovery time for a database by managing dirty page flushing more granularly.
options.C: To verify the integrity of secondary data files.
options.D: To scan the network for unauthorized SQL connections.

questions.question: What is 'Implicit Conversion' and why is it a performance risk?

options.A: It converts users to admins automatically; it is a security risk.
options.B: When types don't match in a join/filter, SQL converts them, often preventing index usage (SARGability).
options.C: It is the process of converting SQL to XML; it is CPU intensive.
options.D: It happens when a database is upgraded; it risks data loss.

questions.question: What is a 'Spinlock'?

options.A: A type of deadlock that happens in the storage engine.
options.B: A lightweight synchronization object used to protect shared data structures in memory.
options.C: A query that loops until the server is restarted.
options.D: A tool used to rotate log files.

questions.question: Which T-SQL statement is used to capture a detailed trace of instance activity using Extended Events?

options.B: START PROFILER

questions.question: What is 'Cost Threshold for Parallelism'?

options.A: The financial cost of running a SQL Server in the cloud.
options.B: The estimated execution cost a query must exceed before a parallel plan is considered.
options.C: The maximum number of users allowed on a parallel server.
options.D: The minimum speed required for the network connection.

questions.question: What is 'Instant File Initialization'?

options.A: A feature that allows SQL Server to start in under 1 second.
options.B: Allows SQL Server to skip zeroing out disk space when growing data files, speeding up file growth.
options.C: A method to initialize variables instantly in T-SQL.
options.D: A way to format a new hard drive from within SSMS.

questions.question: In an execution plan, what does 'Parallelism (Gather Streams)' indicate?

options.A: The query is being split into multiple threads for processing.
options.B: Multiple parallel threads are being merged into a single serial thread for the final output.
options.C: The database is gathering data from multiple remote servers.
options.D: The server is running low on available threads.

questions.question: Which DMV is used to analyze internal memory allocations in SQL Server?

options.B: sys.dm_exec_sessions

questions.question: What is 'Non-SARGable' query?

options.A: A query that has a syntax error in the WHERE clause.
options.B: A query where the engine cannot use an index seek because of an operator or function on the column.
options.C: A query that doesn't return any rows.
options.D: A query that is too long to be stored in the cache.

questions.question: What is 'Table Spool' operator in an execution plan?

options.A: An operator that deletes temporary tables.
options.B: An operator that saves an intermediate result set into TempDB to be reused within the same query.
options.C: A physical device used for database tape backups.
options.D: A tool that counts the number of pages in a table.

questions.question: What is 'Plan Regression'?

options.A: When a query plan is manually moved to an older version.
options.B: When a query performs worse after a new execution plan is generated (often due to stale statistics).
options.C: When a database is rolled back to a previous state.
options.D: When the server hardware is downgraded.

questions.question: What is 'Lazy Writer' background process?

options.A: A developer who doesn't write documentation.
options.B: A system process that flushes old pages from the buffer cache to disk when memory pressure occurs.
options.C: A tool that formats SQL code slowly.
options.D: A process that backs up the database at a low priority.

questions.question: What is 'Residual Predicate'?

options.A: A part of a query that is ignored by the engine.
options.B: A filter condition that cannot be pushed into an index seek and must be evaluated on the resulting rows.
options.C: A security rule that applies to deleted users.
options.D: The remaining part of a query after it has been minified.

questions.question: Which T-SQL hint is used to force a specific Join order?

options.B: OPTION (FORCE ORDER)

questions.question: What is 'Lock Escalation Threshold'?

options.A: The time limit before a lock is released.
options.B: The number of locks (typically 5,000) reached on a single object before SQL Server escalates to a table lock.
options.C: The maximum number of users allowed to lock a table.
options.D: The percentage of memory used by the lock manager.

questions.question: What is 'Buffer Pool Extension'?

options.A: Adding more physical RAM to the server.
options.B: A feature that allows using a non-volatile disk (like an SSD) as an extension of the SQL Server buffer pool.
options.C: Increasing the number of simultaneous user connections.
options.D: A tool to compress the data in the RAM cache.

questions.question: What is 'VLF' (Virtual Log File)?

options.A: A backup of the transaction log stored in the cloud.
options.B: A logical segment within the physical transaction log file.
options.C: A temporary file used for sorting data.
options.D: A log file that is only stored in memory.

questions.question: Which command is used to clear the entire Query Plan Cache for the instance?

options.B: DBCC CLEARDATACACHE

questions.question: What is 'Statistics Histogram'?

options.A: A chart showing the history of the database size.
options.B: A set of values in the statistics object that shows the data distribution for the first column.
options.C: A list of all users who have queried the table.
options.D: A log of all index rebuild operations.

questions.question: What is 'Estimated Number of Rows' in an execution plan?

options.A: The exact number of rows the query will return.
options.B: A prediction made by the optimizer based on available statistics to decide the best execution path.
options.C: The total number of rows in the table.
options.D: A random number used for performance testing.

questions.question: Which DMV shows the currently active locks in the entire SQL instance?

options.B: sys.dm_exec_sessions

questions.question: What is 'Turing-Complete' in the context of T-SQL?

options.A: SQL Server's ability to run on any operating system.
options.B: The fact that T-SQL contains enough control flow logic to solve any computational problem.
options.C: A performance metric developed by Alan Turing.
options.D: The encryption standard used by SQL Server.

questions.question: What is 'Sort Warning' in Extended Events?

options.A: A warning that the result set is not sorted.
options.B: An alert that a sort operation has spilled from memory into TempDB, significantly slowing performance.
options.C: A notification that an ORDER BY clause is missing.
options.D: A warning that the sort column is too wide.

questions.question: What is 'Non-Clustered Columnstore Index' used for?

options.A: To provide high-speed transactional row lookups.
options.B: To allow real-time analytics on transactional tables without creating a separate data warehouse.
options.D: To sort the data on the disk more efficiently.

questions.question: What is 'Query Governor Cost Limit'?

options.A: The maximum price of a SQL Server license.
options.B: A setting to prevent the execution of queries that the optimizer estimates will exceed a certain time threshold.
options.C: The total number of rows a single query can return.
options.D: The maximum CPU temperature allowed during a query.

questions.question: What is 'Auto-Update Statistics Async'?

options.A: A feature that updates statistics every hour automatically.
options.B: A setting that allows a query to execute with old statistics while a background thread updates them.
options.C: A method to update statistics using a separate database server.
options.D: An error that prevents statistics from being updated.

questions.question: What does 'Symmetric Encryption' mean in SQL Server?

options.A: Using two different keys for encryption and decryption.
options.B: Using the same key for both encryption and decryption.
options.C: Encryption that works on all servers equally.
options.D: A method to encrypt data in a symmetrical table.

questions.question: What is 'Transparent Data Encryption' (TDE)?

options.A: Encryption that makes the data visible to everyone.
options.B: Encryption of the entire database files at rest without requiring application-level code changes.
options.C: A method to encrypt only the data sent over the network.
options.D: A feature that removes encryption from the data.

questions.question: Which DMV is best for analyzing TempDB space usage by internal objects?

options.B: sys.dm_exec_query_stats

questions.question: What is 'Cardinality' in database design?

options.A: The total number of tables in a database.
options.B: The measure of the uniqueness of data values in a specific column.
options.C: The speed of the database server.
options.D: The number of users who can access a table.

questions.question: What is 'Database Snapshot' primarily used for?

options.A: To take a physical photograph of the server hardware.
options.B: To create a read-only, point-in-time view of a database for reporting or recovery.
options.C: To back up the database to a secondary cloud provider.
options.D: To monitor the real-time activity of a database.

questions.question: What is 'Hash Match' operator?

options.A: A security feature that hashes passwords.
options.B: A join or aggregation operator that builds a hash table in memory to process large result sets.
options.C: An operator used to compare two identical tables.
options.D: A tool to find duplicate records in a table.

questions.question: What is 'Nested Loops' join?

options.A: A join that runs in a loop until the data is found.
options.B: A join operator that iterates through each row of the outer table and searches for a match in the inner table.
options.C: A join that connects more than three tables.
options.D: A join used only for small numeric columns.

questions.question: What is 'Bitmap Filter' in execution plans?

options.A: A tool to filter images stored in the database.
options.B: An optimization used in parallel queries to eliminate rows that won't qualify for a join early in the process.
options.C: A security filter that blocks certain IP addresses.
options.D: A way to view the database schema as a bitmap image.

questions.question: What is 'Batch Mode' execution?

options.A: Running multiple SQL scripts one after another.
options.B: Processing a set of rows together (vectorized) rather than row-by-row to optimize CPU cache usage.
options.C: A feature for executing queries at night.
options.D: A method to insert data in batches of 1,000.

questions.question: What is 'Wait Type' PAGELATCH_EX?

options.A: An error that a page is missing from the database.
options.B: Contention on a data page in memory, often related to high-concurrency inserts on an identity column.
options.C: A warning that the server is out of disk space.
options.D: A process that flushes old data to the transaction log.

questions.question: What is 'External Pushdown' in PolyBase?

options.A: Pushing data from the cloud to the local server.
options.B: Delegating the execution of a query filter or join to the external data source (like Hadoop or Oracle) to reduce data transfer.
options.C: A method to push security rules to all users.
options.D: Pushing a database backup to an offsite location.
